question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}v\\u\\- u^{2} + v^{2}\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(v)&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- u^{2} + v^{2})&=- 2 u\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(v)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u)&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- u^{2} + v^{2})&=2 v\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\- 2 u\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\2 v\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\0 & 1 & - 2 u\\1 & 0 & 2 v\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(1)(2 v)\\&\quad -(- 2 u)(0)\\&=2 v.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(0)(2 v)\\&\quad +(- 2 u)(1)\\&=- 2 u.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(0)(0)\\&\quad -(1)(1)\\&=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}2 v\\- 2 u\\-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

generation.domain: all real u,v; zero products at singular parameters allowed

question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}- v \cos{(u )}\\\sin{(u )}\\v^{2}\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- v \cos{(u )})&=v \sin{(u )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(\sin{(u )})&=\cos{(u )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(v^{2})&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- v \cos{(u )})&=- \cos{(u )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(\sin{(u )})&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(v^{2})&=2 v\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}v \sin{(u )}\\\cos{(u )}\\0\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}- \cos{(u )}\\0\\2 v\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\v \sin{(u )} & \cos{(u )} & 0\\- \cos{(u )} & 0 & 2 v\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(\cos{(u )})(2 v)\\&\quad -(0)(0)\\&=2 v \cos{(u )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(v \sin{(u )})(2 v)\\&\quad +(0)(- \cos{(u )})\\&=- 2 v^{2} \sin{(u )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(v \sin{(u )})(0)\\&\quad -(\cos{(u )})(- \cos{(u )})\\&=\cos^{2}{(u )}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}2 v \cos{(u )}\\- 2 v^{2} \sin{(u )}\\\cos^{2}{(u )}\end{pmatrix}.
$$

generation.domain: all real u,v; zero products at singular parameters allowed

question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}- v^{2} - 1\\u^{3} + 1\\u - 2 v\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- v^{2} - 1)&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u^{3} + 1)&=3 u^{2}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u - 2 v)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- v^{2} - 1)&=- 2 v\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u^{3} + 1)&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u - 2 v)&=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}0\\3 u^{2}\\1\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}- 2 v\\0\\-2\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\0 & 3 u^{2} & 1\\- 2 v & 0 & -2\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(3 u^{2})(-2)\\&\quad -(1)(0)\\&=- 6 u^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(0)(-2)\\&\quad +(1)(- 2 v)\\&=- 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(0)(0)\\&\quad -(3 u^{2})(- 2 v)\\&=6 u^{2} v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}- 6 u^{2}\\- 2 v\\6 u^{2} v\end{pmatrix}.
$$

generation.domain: all real u,v; zero products at singular parameters allowed
